html:
The Queets were a Salishan people of the Queets River on the Pacific coast of the Olympic Peninsula in Washington. They spoke a dialect of the Quinault language.

They lived by catching salmon in the river, gathering shellfish and hunting sea mammals and elk, and built large cedar plank houses. In the Treaty of Olympia of 1855 to 1856 they were grouped with their neighbours, and today their descendants belong to the Quinault Indian Nation, whose village of Queets stands at the river mouth. Their neighbours to the north include the Quileute and the Hoh.
sum: The Queets were a Salishan people of the Queets River on the Pacific coast of the Olympic Peninsula in Washington. They spoke a dialect of the Quinault language.
